\begin{abstract}
IRexp is a redistributable collection of \textbf{experimental infrared band lists}
(cm$^{-1}$ peak positions) mined from open chemistry literature, optionally with
$^1$H/$^{13}$C shifts and resolved structures.
The release holds \textbf{121,233} records (119,345 PMC OA; 1,888 Chemotion/RADAR4Chem),
with \textbf{43,060} structure-linked and \textbf{33,201} full IR + $^1$H + $^{13}$C + structure
quadruples.
IRexp stores \textbf{numeric band lists}, not absorbance traces.
Records carry \texttt{source\_doi} and stamped \texttt{license} / \texttt{license\_pool}.
Licensing is \textbf{mixed}: Europe PMC join yields \textbf{87,617} commercial (CC-BY/CC0),
\textbf{20,938} non-commercial (NC*), \textbf{10,781} empty/unknown (excluded from commercial
Zenodo), and \textbf{1,897} ShareAlike (Chemotion + rare PMC SA).
Reuse: multimodal training and complementary elucidation benchmarks citing this Descriptor.
Data: Hugging Face \texttt{ilkhamfy/IRexp}; Zenodo DOI pending archival mint.
Code is MIT-licensed.
\end{abstract}

\section{Background \& Summary}

Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is routine in organic characterisation, yet
\textbf{open, redistributable} collections of \emph{experimental} IR data remain sparse
relative to modern machine-learning needs.
Digitised absorbance libraries such as the NIST Chemistry WebBook~\citep{nist_webbook}
and AIST SDBS~\citep{sdbs} are valuable but either modest in size or \textbf{view-only}
(no bulk redistribution).
Computational IR--NMR resources published in \textit{Scientific Data} expand multimodal
coverage with simulated spectra~\citep{zipoli2025uspto}, while large literature mines for
\textbf{NMR} peak lists (notably NMRexp~\citep{wang2025nmrexp}) demonstrate that
peer-reviewed experimental spectral \emph{lists} with DOI traceability are in scope for
this journal.
Concurrent literature corpora that include IR among other modalities
(for example NMRSpec/NMRTrans~\citep{yang2026nmrtrans}) further motivate an
\textbf{IR-focused, redistributable} band-list resource rather than another closed
spectrum archive.

IRexp fills a specific wedge.
Experimental sections of chemistry papers conventionally report per-compound
\textbf{IR band lists} (wavenumbers in cm$^{-1}$) together with $^1$H/$^{13}$C NMR shift lists.
That textual convention is the object language models and many elucidation pipelines consume,
and it is a \textbf{different object} from a digitised spectrum.
IRexp therefore:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Harvests open-access full text from the \textbf{PMC Open Access Subset} bulk S3
        mirror and peak lists from the \textbf{Chemotion} FT-IR deposit.
  \item Extracts deterministic numeric IR band lists (and co-reported NMR strings where present).
  \item Resolves compound names to canonical structures with OPSIN~\citep{lowe2011opsin},
        RDKit~\citep{landrum_rdkit}, and SELFIES~\citep{krenn2020selfies} where possible.
  \item Releases \textbf{extracted numbers only} --- no PDFs, figures, or article full text ---
        with source accessions for attribution.
\end{enumerate}

Among openly redistributable \emph{text-derived IR band lists}, IRexp is large by record
count (121,233).
It does not claim to replace SDBS or NIST absorbance libraries; SDBS alone holds more
structure-linked \emph{spectra} than IRexp holds structure-linked band lists.
The intended reuse is multimodal pretraining, supervised IR$\to$structure modelling on
\texttt{irexp\_resolved}, and as the literature substrate for complementary elucidation
benchmarks described elsewhere (forthcoming ICLR manuscript on IRSpectra-Bench;
cite that work for protocol and model results --- \textbf{not} reproduced here)~\citep{yabbarov2026irspectra}.

\paragraph{What this Data Descriptor does not contain.}
No hypothesis tests, no large-language-model accuracy tables, and no stage-decomposition
of elucidation performance.
Those belong in the complementary research paper.

\section{Methods}

\subsection{Source corpora}

\paragraph{PMC Open Access Subset.}
Primary harvest uses the NCBI PMC OA bulk distribution on Amazon S3
(\texttt{s3://pmc-oa-opendata}, HTTPS endpoint
\texttt{https://pmc-oa-opendata.s3.amazonaws.com})~\citep{pmc_oa}.
\textbf{Harvest window (recoverable from git snapshots):} the bulk S3 IR crawl and
\texttt{seen\_papers} / \texttt{ir\_harvest\_snapshot} artefacts were produced on
\textbf{2026-06-07 (UTC)} (\texttt{scripts/s3\_ir\_harvest.py}; incremental auto-snapshots
that day through $\sim$134,893 raw IR rows).
Chemotion was ingested the same day.
A harvest snapshot records \textbf{188,016} distinct PMC identifiers scanned
(\texttt{data/irexp/seen\_papers.txt.gz}).
The released corpus retains records from \textbf{15,416} unique \texttt{PMC:*} accessions.
Extraction operates on open-access \textbf{plain text} objects at flat S3 keys
\texttt{PMC\{id\}.\{v\}/PMC\{id\}.\{v\}.txt}.
Europe PMC full-text XML is used for some validation re-fetches.
The \textbf{released} IRexp DOIs are exclusively \texttt{PMC:*} accessions or the Chemotion
deposit DOI; no paywalled publisher DOI appears in the 121,233-record file.

\paragraph{Discovery vs \texttt{oa\_comm} / \texttt{oa\_noncomm} packages.}
Identifier discovery used NCBI E-utilities \texttt{esearch} over PMC with an
IR-characterisation query \textbf{and} \texttt{open access[filter]}, then fetched matching
IDs from the flat S3 text layout.
The harvest therefore did \textbf{not} pre-filter by walking the PMC OA Subset's
\texttt{oa\_comm} vs \texttt{oa\_noncomm} vs other package directories.
PMC OA is still \textbf{not} a single licence~\citep{pmc_oa}.
Licence truth for redistribution is applied \textbf{post-hoc}: every unique PMCID in IRexp
(15,416) was joined to Europe PMC \texttt{license} metadata
(\texttt{scripts/join\_pmc\_licences.py}); each record carries \texttt{license} /
\texttt{license\_pool}.
Commercial-use (CC-BY/CC0) rows form the Zenodo / Sci Data primary pool; NC* are held aside;
empty/unknown are \textbf{excluded} from the commercial deposit --- aligning redistributable
intent with the OA commercial/non-commercial distinction via article-level licences rather
than S3 package paths (\texttt{data/NOTICE};
\texttt{docs/scientific\_data/LICENCE\_REMEDIATION.md}).

\paragraph{Chemotion / RADAR4Chem.}
\textbf{1,888} records come from the Chemotion Repository FT-IR collection deposited at
RADAR4Chem (DOI \texttt{10.22000/OGoEQGlsZGElrgst})~\citep{chemotion2024}, licensed
\textbf{CC-BY-SA-4.0}.
Ingest (\texttt{scripts/chemotion\_to\_irexp.py}, 2026-06-07): download the MD5-verified deposit;
for each of \textbf{2,116} ATR-IR analyses, flatten the Quill-delta \texttt{content} field to
plain text; parse an \textbf{author-curated} IR band list with the \textbf{same} regex
extractor and quality gates as the PMC path; resolve the deposit's canonical SMILES with
RDKit $\to$ InChIKey + SELFIES; keep the richest band list per InChIKey; drop the \textbf{8}
molecules already present in the PMC pool $\to$ \textbf{+1,888} new structure-resolved rows.
These are \textbf{not} algorithmic peak-picks from absorbance curves; they are author-entered
experimental band lists from the ELN deposit, denser than typical paper prose
(median \textbf{39} bands vs \textbf{9} for PMC).
Rows carry \texttt{license=CC-BY-SA-4.0} and \texttt{source\_doi} equal to the deposit DOI.

\paragraph{Excluded.}
AIST SDBS (view-only; no bulk export)~\citep{sdbs}; NIST WebBook join code exists in the
repository but contributes \textbf{0} records to the released IRexp
(\texttt{ir\_source} is always \texttt{experimental} for released rows).

\subsection{Discovery and fetch (released corpus)}

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Discover IR-reporting OA PMCIDs via NCBI \texttt{esearch}
        (\texttt{open access[filter]} + characterisation-format IR query; year/month sliced).
  \item Fetch OA full text from PMC-OA S3 plain-text objects (\texttt{PMC\{id\}.\{v\}.txt}).
  \item Ingest Chemotion deposit author-curated band lists + structures
        (\texttt{scripts/chemotion\_to\_irexp.py}).
  \item Persist harvest provenance in \texttt{seen\_papers.txt.gz} and optional rawer rows in
        \texttt{ir\_harvest\_snapshot.jsonl.gz} (134,893 rows including intermediate prose fields;
        the curated release is \texttt{irexp.jsonl.gz}).
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Non-OA / Scrapling fence.}
Development adapters for ChemRxiv, Beilstein, and generic publisher pages exist for exploration.
They are \textbf{outside the construction path of the released dataset}.
\textbf{No released \texttt{source\_doi} is a paywalled publisher DOI.}
Methods for IRexp as published here cite only \textbf{PMC-OA S3 + Chemotion}.

\subsection{Extraction (band lists, not spectra)}

A deterministic regular-expression pipeline (\texttt{spectro\_scraper/extract.py}) segments
experimental text per compound and extracts:
\begin{itemize}
  \item IR wavenumbers $\to$ \texttt{ir\_bands\_cm-1} (list of floats, cm$^{-1}$);
  \item $^1$H and $^{13}$C payloads $\to$ \texttt{h\_nmr} / \texttt{c\_nmr} (author strings, when present).
\end{itemize}
Gates reject scan-range artefacts and common prose false positives.
\textbf{No curve digitisation} is performed: figures are not traced; JCAMP-DX is not stored.

\subsection{Structure resolution}

Where an IUPAC or systematic name is available, names are converted with
OPSIN~\citep{lowe2011opsin}, canonicalised with RDKit~\citep{landrum_rdkit}, and encoded as
InChIKey and SELFIES~\citep{krenn2020selfies}.
An optional PubChem~\citep{kim2023pubchem} name fallback (\texttt{USE\_PUBCHEM}) handles
trivial names.
Structure coverage of the full release is \textbf{35.5\%} (43,060 / 121,233).
The structure-complete split is shipped as \texttt{irexp\_resolved}.

\subsection{Quality tooling}

Optional physics gates live in \texttt{spectro\_scraper/quality.py}
($^{13}$C peak count $\leq$ carbon count; $^1$H integration vs formula; IR wavenumber windows).
They were \textbf{not} applied as a hard filter at harvest; Technical Validation reports a
full-corpus post-hoc quarantine on \texttt{irexp\_resolved}
(\texttt{scripts/quarantine\_structure\_nmr.py} $\to$
\texttt{data/audit/structure\_nmr\_quarantine.jsonl.gz}).
Transcription and recall-proxy scripts: \texttt{scripts/audit\_extraction.py},
\texttt{scripts/audit\_extraction\_recall.py}.

\section{Data Records}

\subsection{Object definition}

Each IRexp record is a JSON object.
Required chemistry fields for an IR entry:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llp{7.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Field & Type & Description \\
\midrule
\texttt{id} & string & Stable record id (InChIKey when resolved, else internal) \\
\texttt{ir\_bands\_cm-1} & float list & Experimental IR peak positions (cm$^{-1}$) \\
\texttt{ir\_source} & string & \texttt{experimental} for all released rows \\
\texttt{source\_doi} & string & \texttt{PMC:<pmcid>} or Chemotion deposit DOI \\
\texttt{h\_nmr} / \texttt{c\_nmr} & string or null & Author-reported shift lists \\
\texttt{smiles} / \texttt{selfies} / \texttt{inchikey} & string or null & Resolved structure encodings \\
\texttt{has\_structure} & bool & Convenience flag \\
\texttt{license} / \texttt{license\_pool} & string & Per-article stamp (Europe PMC join or Chemotion) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\textbf{Not included:} absorbance traces, intensities, instrument metadata beyond what
appears in source text, PDFs, figures, or full article bodies.

\section{Technical Validation}

Machine-readable package: \texttt{docs/scientific\_data/qc\_structure\_nmr.json}
(and artefacts under \texttt{data/audit/}).

\subsection{Transcription fidelity (PMC)}

On a seed-fixed random sample of \textbf{60} PMC-sourced records
(\texttt{scripts/audit\_extraction.py --n 60 --seed 0}), each article was re-fetched from
Europe PMC and every recorded wavenumber was checked against the source text
($\pm$1\,cm$^{-1}$ integer match).
Result: \textbf{560/560 bands} and \textbf{60/60 records} confirmed.
Enlarged sample \textbf{n=200} (same script/seed family,
\texttt{data/audit/extraction\_audit\_n200.json}): \textbf{2,250/2,261 bands (99.51\%)} and
\textbf{196/200 records (98.0\%)} fully confirmed.
This bounds \textbf{transcription} error (hallucinated, mis-parsed, or unit-mangled values).

\subsection{Extraction-recall proxy (PMC, harvest path)}

A human mark-up of every IR string in every paper remains the gold standard.
As an automatic \textbf{proxy} on the actual harvest path
(\texttt{scripts/audit\_extraction\_recall.py --n 40 --seed 0}): re-fetch PMC-OA S3 plain text
for \textbf{40} distinct source PMCIDs; re-run \texttt{extract\_records}; compare band-sets to
released rows ($\pm$1\,cm$^{-1}$).
Result: \textbf{2,640/2,640} released bands confirmed in re-extract; \textbf{248/248} released
IR lists recovered (list-level recall proxy \textbf{1.0}; 40/40 papers); \textbf{4/40} papers
yielded \emph{extra} re-extracted lists relative to the curated release
(parser over-fire vs post-harvest dedup/curation, not missed released compounds).
Summary: \texttt{data/audit/extraction\_recall\_proxy.json}.
This is \textbf{not} a substitute for expert human recall.

\subsection{Structure--NMR consistency and quarantine (resolved)}

\paragraph{Sample (prior).}
On \textbf{500} \texttt{irexp\_resolved} records with $^{13}$C text (seed 0):
\textbf{17/500 (3.4\%)} listed more peaks than carbons.
On \textbf{500} with $^1$H text: integrals $>$ formula H+2 in \textbf{17/497 (3.4\%)}.

\paragraph{Full resolved corpus.}
\texttt{scripts/quarantine\_structure\_nmr.py} applied the same physics gates to all
\textbf{43,060} structure-linked rows.
\textbf{1,882 (4.37\%)} fail $\geq$1 hard check and are listed in
\texttt{data/audit/structure\_nmr\_quarantine.jsonl.gz} (diagnostic only --- release files
unchanged).
Among rows with the relevant modality: $^{13}$C peaks $>$ carbons
\textbf{1,194/34,231 (3.49\%)}; $^1$H integral $>$ formula+2
\textbf{1,141/39,672 (2.88\%)}; IR out-of-range \textbf{0}; unparseable SMILES \textbf{0}.
Re-users should filter quarantined IDs before supervised training.
These rates are integrity diagnostics, \textbf{not} an expert skeleton audit.

\subsection{IR physical window}

Every band in the full 121,233-record release lies in \textbf{[350, 4000]\,cm$^{-1}$}
(0 / 1,360,866 out of range).

\section{Usage Notes}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Band lists $\neq$ spectra.} Do not evaluate models trained on IRexp as if they
        had seen full absorbance curves.
  \item \textbf{Separate pools by density and licence.} PMC (sparse, author-transcribed) vs
        Chemotion (denser, author-curated ELN band lists).
        Keep Chemotion ShareAlike constraints in mind when combining pools; combined
        redistribution of Chemotion-derived rows must honour CC-BY-SA-4.0.
  \item \textbf{Do not assume PMC = CC-BY-4.0.} Filter to
        \texttt{license\_pool == "commercial"} (or use \texttt{irexp\_commercial.jsonl.gz})
        for commercial redistribution; attribute via \texttt{source\_doi} / \texttt{pmcid}.
  \item \textbf{Structure--NMR quarantine.} Before supervised training on
        \texttt{irexp\_resolved}, optionally drop IDs in
        \texttt{data/audit/structure\_nmr\_quarantine.jsonl.gz} ($\sim$4.4\% of resolved rows).
  \item \textbf{Training without benchmark leakage.} If using the complementary IRSpectra-Bench
        problems, fine-tune from \texttt{train\_no\_bench.jsonl.gz} (or rebuild with
        \texttt{scripts/build\_train\_no\_bench.py}) so benchmark InChIKeys are withheld.
  \item \textbf{Structure coverage.} Prefer \texttt{irexp\_resolved} for supervised structure
        tasks; 64.5\% of records lack SMILES.
  \item \textbf{Attribution.} Cite this Data Descriptor / Zenodo DOI and attribute originating
        articles through each record's \texttt{source\_doi}.
\end{itemize}
